specialty: statistics: recompute p-values, CIs, multiplicity handling and power claims from the shipped evidence
summary: The paper argues that a multiple-choice score should be tested against the construct's best constant, input-blind predictor before any arm-vs-arm comparison, and that this floor is itself an estimate needing its own calibration against a null the construct can realise. It contributes (i) a nine-construct floor table with a legality-aware winner's-curse calibration, (ii) an enumeration of four degrees of freedom in the content floor (tie convention, length unit, tokenizer, meaning of 'chance' under variable n_opt), (iii) an arm-conditional within-n_opt-stratum permutation null (read-out v2) used as a pre-comparison gate, and (iv) a large MMLU-Pro demonstration that under structural damage 15/17 designated damaged cells sit at or below their arm-independent floor while most read above a chance line. I recomputed essentially every statistic I could reach from the 17 shipped evidence paths and the reproduction rate is unusually high: 1403/12032 = 0.11660571808510638 rounds to the printed 0.116606; mean(1/n_opt) over the shipped histogram {3:21,4:606,5:52,6:93,7:158,8:320,9:801,10:9981} is 0.11087694718844986 -> 0.110877; the gap/ratio pairs (+1.661pp, 1.1661x) and (+0.573pp, 1.0517x) are exact; all 13 per-cell deltas in Table 5 (tab_mmlupro) reproduce from acc - 1403/12032 to within 0.001pp; the BH step-up over the 27 v2 cells gives exactly q=0.0297 for qwen3/k14 (rank 6) and q=0.0663 for olmo2/keep14 (rank 7, threshold 7*0.05/27=0.0130), with 6 cells at q<=0.05 and 5 clearing Bonferroni 0.05/27=0.001852, all as printed; the binomial P(X>=3 | 12, 0.05) = 0.019568 -> 0.0196; shortgpt16's '5.2x its own half-width' is 3.6735/0.70229 = 5.231; qwen3/k14's recovery 0.0493/0.5441 = 9.05% -> '9.1%'; the 623-item four-stratum count and the exactly-36-item / 0.299pp stratification slack are exact; the tightest v2 margin is llama2/k12 at 0.007784pp, matching the stated 0.0078; every delta and half-width in Table 4 (tab_power) reproduces from the gate2 CSV CI endpoints; and the length-unit claims (max |d split| = 2.0202, |d credit| in 14.527-35.201, ARC-C ties 0.18601 char vs 0.50853 token) all reproduce. The 45/85 and 9/85 off-MMLU counts also close arithmetically: the shipped OLMo-2 leg gives 20/25 above chance and 9/25 above floor, which with the stated non-OLMo 25/60 and 0/60 sums to exactly 45 and 9. The paper's self-auditing is genuinely unusual -- it withdraws its own flagship row (MMLU-Pro p 0.0 -> 0.083) because its original null was outside the construct's legal support, reports two rows that moved in its favour, and separately corrects a floor-rounding convention that biased p downward. My objections are therefore not about arithmetic. They are: (a) the power criterion 'achieved CI95 half-width < the reference effect' is a 50%-power criterion, not the 80% the word 'powered' will be read as, and the paper's own reference effect is itself an interval estimate; (b) the BH family that produces the surviving downgrade is selected in a way that changes the answer -- dropping the four intact anchors, which are guaranteed rejections and are not damaged arms, moves qwen3/k14 to q=0.076; (c) the symmetric-standard flip is 3/12 vs 1/12 and the paper's own binomial instrument gives P(X>=1|12,0.05)=0.46 for the floor side, so the corrected comparison is 'chance side not uniformly null, floor side indistinguishable from null', which is weaker than the text implies; and (d) two evidence files that the shipped claim map names as the sources of headline claims H-02 and H-04 (evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json, evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json) are absent from the snapshot, and neither the fp32-precision paragraph's numbers (4,303 ties, 2,532 flips, 18.03%, McNemar p=0.5702, CI [-0.0064,+0.0033]) nor the per-stratum argmax letters (B,E,B,E) and 1439/12032 have any machine-readable home among the 17 shipped paths. The reproducibility statement's central assurance -- '610 numerals with none unresolved' -- is not checkable here: the shipped checker exits 0 having scanned 0 files, and it in fact reads the superseded floor_winners_curse_calibration.json rather than the corrected E-CAL record.
strengths: The headline arithmetic reproduces at full precision from the shipped evidence, which is rare. Table 5 (manuscript/tab_mmlupro.tex): all 13 printed deltas equal acc - 1403/12032 to <0.001pp (e.g. shortgpt16 0.153341 -> +3.6735 vs printed +3.674; llama2/k8 0.107463 -> -0.9143 vs -0.914). Table 1 (tab_nulls.tex) floors, chances, gaps and ratios all match evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json rows[] exactly. Table 4 (tab_power.tex): all six keep8 deltas and all six half-widths recompute from the ci95_lo/ci95_hi columns of evidence/second_mc_benchmark/gate2_letter_content_nulls.csv (arc_challenge -0.9386/3.8822, openbookqa -1.8000/6.4000, etc.).

The self-falsification of the flagship row is real and correctly reasoned, not cosmetic. Appendix Sec. 'The calibrating null must be realisable' (03b_nulls.tex:30-41) withdraws MMLU-Pro from 'above balanced null' because the original null drew gold letters uniformly over ten letters while 2051/12032 items (17.05%, which I verified from the shipped n_opt histogram) cannot carry gold letter J. The corrected E[f-hat] moves 0.104457 -> 0.113873 and p 0.0 -> 0.083, and I confirm from evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:rows[0].big_run_aware that p_exact_floor=0.082948 over 1e6 draws with per-seed spread 0.082355-0.083445 across three seeds and 0.08455 under an independent per-item categorical implementation.

The directionality of the correction is measured and reported against the authors' interest, including the two rows that moved in their favour. evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:directionality contradicts an earlier internal claim of universal monotonicity, and the manuscript prints it (03b_nulls.tex:37): ARC-Easy 0.140->0.136 and ARC-Challenge 0.453->0.447. The shipped per-row dE_max_sigma of -9.78 and -17.75 confirm these are real rather than Monte-Carlo, and the second, smaller floor-rounding defect (comparing against a 6-dp floor demands count 1404 when 1403 was observed, biasing p down: MMLU-Pro 0.0776 -> 0.0831, PIQA 0.6557 -> 0.6895) is disclosed with the same sign discipline.

The constant-collapse identity for read-out v2 is verified numerically, not asserted. evidence/heal_readout_v2_permutation_null.json:selftest_collapse_invariance shows always-L acc == acc_hat, delta_perm_pp = 0.0 for all ten letters A-J, each conditioned on the items where that letter is legal (n_items 12032 down to 9981 for J). This closes the 'collapse onto a different letter' loophole that the paper correctly identifies as the failure mode of using a best-constant floor as a competence test (03_method.tex:23).

The v1/v2 ordering is presented as a measured property under an explicit regularity condition rather than as a theorem, with the violating construction exhibited. Appendix app:ordering (09a_relocated.tex:15): I verified the four-stratum count (n_opt 5,6,7,8 sizes 52+93+158+320 = 623), the per-stratum-argmax sum 1439/12032 giving exactly 36 items = 0.2992pp of slack, and that the tightest cell is indeed llama2/k12 at f_const - acc_hat = 0.007784pp. I also confirmed the paper's own deflation of its evidence: 13 of 27 cells clear the floor by more than the 0.299pp slack and so could not have violated the bound under any prediction vector, leaving 14 binding cells of which 5 are one healing run sampled 500 steps apart -- exactly as stated.

The claim ledger (Table 9, tab_claims.tex) and the integrity table (Table 8, tab_integrity.tex) make the retraction history and three repaired defects legible, and the bootstrap repair in evidence/R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md correctly diagnoses the illegal p=1.042 as a double-counted zero atom (p = 2*min((bs<=0).mean(), (bs>=0).mean()) with both tails including bs==0) rather than a missing clamp, and documents that exactly three field paths moved with 0/24 verdicts and 0/30 threshold crossings.
weaknesses: The power criterion is a 50%-power criterion described with the word 'powered'. Sec. 4 'Power design' (04_experiments.tex:19-20) and evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json:power_verdict.criterion both define adequacy as 'achieved CI95 half-width < 1.389 pp', the MMLU reference effect. But hw = effect means the effect sits exactly at the CI boundary, i.e. power = 0.500 at alpha=0.05, not 0.80. Conventional 80% power needs hw <= 1.389*1.96/2.8025 = 0.9714 pp. Under that standard the widest MMLU-Pro cell (hw = 0.9684) clears by 0.003 pp -- so the 21/21 claim survives, but barely, and by luck rather than by design. In Table 4 the criterion is actively misleading: ARC-Easy (hw = 1.305) is labelled 'yes, borderline' at power 0.550, Winogrande (hw = 1.184) is labelled 'yes' at power 0.633, and MMLU itself -- the row labelled 'reference' -- has hw = 1.154, i.e. power 0.655 for its own effect. Please either restate the criterion as 'the effect lies outside the achieved interval' (which is what it is) or recompute the table at 80%.

The reference effect against which everything is powered is itself an interval estimate, and the paper never propagates that. -1.389 pp carries hw = 1.154 (Table 4, first row), so its own 95% interval is [-2.543, -0.235] pp. Powering to the point estimate is powering to the middle of a range that reaches 0.235 pp; requiring 80% power at that end needs hw <= 0.1644 pp, which only 2 of the 21 MMLU-Pro letter cells achieve (llama2/k14 and k12, both hw = 0.0831). This does not overturn the paper's use of MMLU-Pro, but 'all 21 evaluated cells are powered at the scale of the reference effect' (abstract; 04_experiments.tex:20) should say which scale, and the sentence 'OLMo-2 keep8's interval excludes an MMLU-sized below-floor effect' (06_discussion.tex:12) needs the same qualification -- keep8's hw is 0.5818, which excludes -1.389 but not -0.235.

The BH family that produces the paper's one surviving downgrade is selected in a way that changes the verdict, and the paper's defence of the family choice does not address this. Sec. 5.3 (05_analysis.tex:41) calls the 27 cells 'the one place in this paper where the family definition is not in dispute: one table, one null, one statistic, one item set'. But four of the 27 are intact base models with p = 0.0001 and delta_perm from +1.959 to +34.889 pp -- guaranteed rejections that are not damaged arms and are not part of any scientific question the table asks. Recomputing BH after removing exactly those four (m=23): qwen3/k14 moves from q = 0.0297 to q = 0.0759 and no longer survives correction, and the count of q<=0.05 cells drops from 6 to 1. So the sentence 'The downgrade survives correction' is a statement about a family that includes four cells inserted to anchor the scale. Conversely, collapsing the five qwen3 heal@5000..7000 checkpoints of one run (500 steps apart, five separate BH slots) to one representative gives m=23 with q = 0.0253 -- still surviving. The honest presentation is both sensitivity analyses, since the two adjustments to the same family push in opposite directions.

The symmetric-standard result is reported as 'the flip survives' when the paper's own instrument says only that the chance side is non-null. Sec. 5.1 (05_analysis.tex:23-25) reports 3/12 vs 1/12 and then, in app:analysis-mult (09a_relocated.tex:37), that under BH or Bonferroni neither reference retains a cell, falling back on P(X>=3|12,0.05) = 0.0196 (which I reproduce). But applying that same binomial to the floor side gives P(X>=1|12,0.05) = 0.4596. So the corrected statement is asymmetric in the opposite direction from the one the paper is correcting: the chance side is not uniformly null, and the floor side is not distinguishable from the global null at all. The text 'the flip survives a symmetric test but is about a third of its advertised size' (05_analysis.tex:23) understates this; the honest reading is that after multiplicity the two references cannot be compared as counts, only as an asymmetry in the number of rejections.

Two evidence files that the shipped claim map designates as the sources of headline claims are not in the snapshot, so the two most load-bearing statistical claims cannot be verified from the artifact. evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv row H-02 ('the flip is 3/12 vs 1/12, NOT 10/12 vs 1/12') cites evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json, and row H-04 (the v1/v2 ordering) cites evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json. Neither exists under the snapshot's evidence/ directory. I could reconstruct 3/12 vs 1/12 only approximately: from evidence/mmlu_scale_power/mmlu_pro_power_nulls_v2.json I get 10/12 point-above-chance-mean and 12/12 above naive 0.10 exactly, and 3/12 above floor with 1/12 CI-excluding, but the chance-side CI column exists nowhere in the shipped evidence (grep for vs_chance / chance_ci95 / chance_boot_p returns 0 hits across all 17 paths), so the 3/12 in the CI column of the Sec. 5.1 table is unverifiable here. Similarly the per-stratum argmax letters B,E,B,E and the value 1439/12032 in app:ordering appear in no shipped file (I had to derive 1439-1403=36 from the printed claim itself, which is circular).

The reproducibility statement's central assurance is not reproducible from the shipped code, and the shipped checker points at the superseded evidence file. 10_reproducibility.tex:4-7 says 'A checker walks all numerals in the source and requires each to be either an exact match to a value in the evidence set, a correct rounding of one, or a stated difference of two; at the time of writing it reports 610 numerals with none unresolved.' Running the shipped code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py in the snapshot exits rc=0 having scanned 0 files ('[scan] 0 files, 21 targets ... n_checked=0 n_ok=0 n_mismatch=0 n_uncovered=12') because it globs PAPER/sections/*.tex, a directory that does not exist here, and code/emit_tab_construct_nulls.py --check-only exits rc=1 with FileNotFoundError on evidence/e2_single_source_assertion.json. Worse, check_prose_vs_evidence.py:92 sets CALIB = evidence/floor_winners_curse_calibration.json -- the file that construct_nulls_legality_aware.json explicitly supersedes -- so the checker the paper points to as its integrity binding validates prose against the withdrawn calibration. A checker that returns green over zero inputs is not evidence, and neither the 610 count nor 'none unresolved' can be confirmed.

The fp32-precision subsection has no machine-readable home in the snapshot, and it is the one place the paper makes a causal-mechanism claim. Sec. 5.4 (05_analysis.tex:51) states 4,303 bf16 exact top-two ties, 2,532 of 14,042 argmax changes (I confirm 2532/14042 = 0.18032 -> the printed 18.03%), accuracy change -0.0015 with CI95 [-0.0064,+0.0033] and exact McNemar p = 0.5702, and floor deltas -1.538 pp (p = 0.0060) fp32 versus -1.389 pp (p = 0.0190) bf16. Of these, only the two p-values appear anywhere in the shipped evidence (evidence/R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md, which reports keep8 letter_vs_null 0.0192 -> 0.0190 bf16 and 0.0062 -> 0.0060 fp32); grep across all 17 paths finds no 4303-as-tie-count, no 2532-as-flip-count, no 18.03, no 0.5702 and no 0.0033. The E-provenance table (Table 10, app:provenance) routes this claim through tcodex_out/EVIDENCE_PACK.md, which is outside the artifact. Since this is the paragraph that rules out a competing explanation for the whole measurement failure, it needs a shipped per-item record.

The multiplicity discussion is honest but the paper still leans on 'the exceptions are concentrated' as a substitute for correction, and that concentration claim is partly structural rather than empirical. app:designated (09a_relocated.tex:26) argues that 'a test that failed indiscriminately would not place all of its rejections at one end of the damage ladder', citing 9/85 off-MMLU with all nine at >=14 retained layers. But from the shipped gate2 CSV those nine are 5 shortgpt16 cells (16/32 layers) and 4 keep14 cells, i.e. two arms, and the comparison group at the same retained depth of 14 in the three truncation families is 0/15 -- which the appendix itself concedes means the threshold is 'a property of the healed ladder, not of depth alone'. With OLMo-2 the only prune-then-heal family, 'concentrated at one end of the damage ladder' and 'concentrated in the only family that was healed' are not separable in this design, so the concentration argument cannot carry the weight of the missing family-wise correction.

Two smaller reporting issues. (a) The claim map is stale relative to the manuscript in a way that touches a headline: claim_evidence_map.tsv row H-03 still reads 'NARROWED to 3 constructs / only MMLU-Pro, MMLU, BoolQ survive', while the abstract now correctly says 'only two of the eight letter constructs (MMLU, BoolQ)', and row C-13 still says '14/15' where tab_claims.tex row 13 says 15/17. Since the map is shipped as evidence E-K and Table 9's caption asserts a one-to-one correspondence with it, this is an internal contradiction in the artifact. (b) evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:environment states cross_node_bit_identity is NOT CLAIMED because the five nodes carry three numpy versions with differing same-seed streams; the p-values in Table 1 are therefore node-conditional at the ~1e-3 level (the shipped per-seed spread on MMLU-Pro is 0.082355-0.083445), which is fine for a p reported to 3 dp but should be stated where the seed is stated rather than only in the JSON.
questions: Will you restate the power criterion? Specifically: does 'powered at the scale of the reference effect' mean (i) the reference effect lies outside the achieved CI95, which is what hw < 1.389 pp encodes and corresponds to 50% power, or (ii) 80% power, which needs hw <= 0.9714 pp? Under (ii) the widest MMLU-Pro cell clears by 0.003 pp of half-width; under (i) Table 4's 'yes' for Winogrande is power 0.633 and 'reference' for MMLU is power 0.655. Please print the achieved power per row.

Since -1.389 pp is a point estimate with CI95 [-2.543, -0.235] pp, would you report the power calculation at both ends? At the lower magnitude only 2/21 cells reach 80%. Does any conclusion change if 'MMLU-sized' is read as the CI lower bound rather than the point?

Please add the BH sensitivity analysis for the 27-cell family. Removing the four intact anchors (guaranteed rejections, not damaged arms) gives m=23 and qwen3/k14 at q = 0.0759, i.e. the downgrade does not survive; collapsing the five qwen3 heal@ checkpoints of one run to one gives m=23 and q = 0.0253, i.e. it does. Both are defensible readings of 'one table, one null, one statistic, one item set'. Which family is pre-registered, and what does the paper claim if the anchors are excluded?

In app:analysis-mult you use P(X>=3|12,0.05) = 0.0196 to argue the chance side is not uniformly null. Applying the same instrument to the floor side gives P(X>=1|12,0.05) = 0.4596. Should the corrected sentence be 'the chance side is non-null while the floor side is indistinguishable from the global null', and if so does 'the flip survives a symmetric test' still hold?

Where are evidence/s2_03_symmetric_inference.json and evidence/s2_02_stratified_ordering.json? Your own claim_evidence_map.tsv names them as the sources for H-02 (3/12 vs 1/12) and H-04 (the ordering). Neither is in the artifact, and the chance-side CI column of the Sec. 5.1 table appears in no shipped file.

Where is the per-item record behind Sec. 5.4? 4,303 ties, 2,532 flips, 18.03%, CI95 [-0.0064,+0.0033] and McNemar p = 0.5702 have no machine-readable home in the 17 shipped paths (only the 0.0060/0.0190 pair does, via R7_BOOTSTRAP_P_FIX.md). Likewise the per-stratum argmax letters B,E,B,E and the value 1439/12032 in app:ordering.

The reproducibility statement's '610 numerals with none unresolved' is not reproducible: code/check_prose_vs_evidence.py exits 0 having scanned 0 files in the released layout, and its CALIB constant reads the superseded floor_winners_curse_calibration.json rather than construct_nulls_legality_aware.json. Will you repoint the checker at the corrected E-CAL record, make it fail on zero inputs, and ship the resulting JSON?

Given that OLMo-2 is the only prune-then-heal family and that 0/15 truncation cells at retained depth 14 clear a floor while keep14 clears 4/5, on what basis is 'the exceptions are concentrated at one end of the damage ladder' distinguishable from 'the exceptions are concentrated in the only healed family'? If it is not, does the concentration argument still substitute for family-wise correction?

Will you reconcile claim_evidence_map.tsv with the manuscript? H-03 still says three constructs survive (abstract says two) and C-13 still says 14/15 (tab_claims says 15/17), while Table 9's caption asserts one-to-one correspondence with that map.
what_would_change_my_score: Upward to 8: (1) restate the power criterion in terms of achieved power and print it per row in Table 4, or relabel it as 'effect outside the achieved interval' -- no new experiments needed, the half-widths are already shipped; (2) add the BH family sensitivity analysis (m=27 as printed, m=23 without the four intact anchors, m=23 with the one-run checkpoint series collapsed) and state which family was pre-registered, adjusting the 'survives correction' sentence to whatever holds across all three; (3) apply the binomial instrument symmetrically in app:analysis-mult and rewrite the 'flip survives' sentence accordingly; (4) ship s2_02, s2_03 and a per-item record for the fp32 subsection, or drop the numbers that only those files support; (5) repoint check_prose_vs_evidence.py at construct_nulls_legality_aware.json, make it exit non-zero on zero scanned files, and ship its output JSON so the '610 numerals' assurance becomes checkable; (6) reconcile claim_evidence_map.tsv rows H-03 and C-13 with the current manuscript. Downward to 5: if the chance-side CI column that produces 3/12 turns out not to have been computed as described (a paired item bootstrap with the reference recomputed inside each resample), or if the fp32 numbers cannot be traced to a per-item record, since Sec. 5.4 is the paper's only mechanism-exclusion argument and Sec. 5.1's symmetric table is the correction the paper advertises as its main honesty improvement over its own earlier draft.
blindness_breach_observed: No target score, author-side reviewer notes, or instructions telling me what to conclude were present in the manuscript, code, or evidence I read. Three near-misses that I judge are NOT breaches: (i) main.tex:25-32, main.tex:39-44 and 09_appendix.tex:3-8 carry LaTeX comments about the ICLR page budget that cite internal filenames (paperC/C9_APPLIED_20260816.md, paperC/gate/venue_page_limit.json) and record which passages were relocated to the appendix -- these disclose an editorial process and a repository name but state no target score and give no instruction to a reviewer; (ii) evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:why names 'four of six round_04 blind reviewers (X1/X2/X5/X6)' as having flagged the legality defect, and rollup.DENOMINATOR_FIX_20260816.why cites 'round_04 R1-01' -- this reveals that prior review rounds exist and that specific reviewer IDs raised specific issues, which is provenance for a correction rather than steering, but it does tell me what earlier reviewers found and a stricter blinding protocol would strip it; (iii) evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware.json:directionality and :headline contain author-side editorial directives about presentation ('the blanket claim no row moves in the authors favour is false and must not be printed'; 'It must NOT be described as well inside the estimator noise'). These are self-imposed honesty constraints, not instructions to me, and I did not follow them as guidance -- I independently recomputed the p-values, the per-seed spread and the directionality signs before reading them. I flag all three so the authors can decide whether round-04 reviewer IDs and author-facing directives belong inside a released evidence file.
